_comment: Shared query plan for the RPC / query-performance benchmark dimension.
Used IDENTICALLY against both engines (tron-goblin-node and clean java-tron)
over the java-tron-compatible HTTP /wallet/* JSON API on port 8090.
Every query is read-only and deterministic over the pristine LiteFullNode
snapshot at head 83,316,752 (block-index, account, tx-info, and VM read
paths). Values were picked to fall inside that snapshot's range so both
engines resolve the same data.
Schema per query:
type        - stable id, surfaced in the result JSON
path        - HTTP path, identical on both engines
method      - GET or POST
body        - JSON request body (POST only); omitted for GET
concurrency - list of concurrency levels to sweep
duration_s  - seconds to drive load at each concurrency level
resolve     - optional: a field the runner fills in at startup from a
live query (so a real, in-snapshot value is always used)
The `gettransactionbyid` value is a PLACEHOLDER. The load generator
resolves a real tx id from `getblockbynum` (block_for_num) at startup and
substitutes it; the literal below is the documented fallback if that block
carries no transactions (it does -- mainnet blocks here hold hundreds --
but the resolve step keeps the plan robust across snapshots).
Block / tx choice for THIS snapshot: the source is a LiteFullNode snapshot
(head 83,316,752) that PRUNES historical blocks and DROPS the transaction-
info / receipt stores entirely (transactionRetStore / transactionHistory-
Store are empty). So:
* block_for_num is 83,300,000 -- comfortably inside the retained tail
(blocks below ~83,260,000 are pruned; 83,000,000 is NOT present);
* the tx-lookup query is `gettransactionbyid` (reads the populated `trans`
store -- real data) rather than `gettransactioninfobyid` (which returns
null for every tx on this snapshot because receipts are pruned). Both
are read-only /wallet/* endpoints both engines expose identically;
gettransactionbyid is the one that returns real data here. On a full-
archive snapshot, swap to gettransactioninfobyid for the receipt path.
